name: Namor McKenzie

summary: Namor was created by writer-artist Bill Everett, and his very first story was not a Timely comic at all. Everett drew an eight-page, black-and-white Sub-Mariner tale for Motion Picture Funnies Weekly #1, a promotional book that the independent studio Funnies Inc. put together as a giveaway for cinemas in the spring of 1939. The Marvel Fandom wiki lists it with a June 1939 cover date and an April 1939 release, but notes that it was never actually distributed and that few people knew it existed until 1974. The same pages were then reprinted in colour as the opening of a longer Sub-Mariner story in Marvel Comics #1 (cover-dated October 1939, on sale at the end of August), the first comic from the company then known as Timely and later as Marvel. That is why the wiki gives Motion Picture Funnies Weekly #1 as his first appearance and Marvel Comics #1 as his first Marvel/Timely appearance.

In that debut Namor is no hero. He kills two salvage divers searching a wreck, cripples their ship and carries the bodies home, where his mother, Princess Fen, explains the grudge: in 1920 a polar expedition ship, the Oracle, set off explosives in Antarctica that killed many of their people. Fen, who could pass for human, went aboard to investigate, fell in love with its commander, Leonard McKenzie, and became pregnant; when the undersea people attacked the ship anyway, the sailors nearly wiped them out. Twenty years on, Namor is starting his people's war of revenge, and he closes the story wrecking a lighthouse with his cousin Dorma. Later retellings, among them Fantastic Four Annual #1 (1963), Sub-Mariner #1 (1968) and Saga of the Sub-Mariner #1 (1988), filled in the gaps: his name means 'Avenging Son', Fen married McKenzie before a raiding party dragged her home believing him dead, and his people were only called Atlanteans, and drawn blue-skinned, from 1963.

As the child of a human and an Atlantean, Namor grew up unlike anyone else in the kingdom: flashback stories show him breathing air for as long as he likes, showing strength and toughness beyond other Atlanteans and, at about fourteen, sprouting the small ankle wings that let him fly. The wiki treats him as a hybrid who is also a mutant, and he is often billed as Marvel's first mutant, although the wiki points out that several mutants are older in story time. The MCU keeps the ankle wings, the pointed ears and a mother named Fen, but changes almost everything else. There he is born in 1571 among Mesoamerican refugees in the Yucatán who survived smallpox brought by Spanish conquerors by eating a vibranium-laced plant, he never knows his father, his kingdom is Talokan rather than an Antarctic Atlantis, and he takes the name Namor from a dying Spanish priest's insult, 'el niño sin amor'.

comics.title: The Avenging Son
comics.summary: After his first raids Namor heads for New York, smashing property and killing police officers while chasing a socialite who has caught his eye. Officer Betty Dean is sent to lure him into a trap, but instead she watches him sink a Nazi U-boat that is attacking a British freighter, and he begins to turn on the Axis. A spell in the courts ends with a death sentence that the electric chair only recharges, and his renewed attack on the city in 1940 brings a running battle with the android Human Torch across several issues that Betty finally talks both of them out of. In his own Sub-Mariner Comics #1 he leads his people against a Nazi submarine fleet bombing their undersea home.

comics.title: War hero, revival and amnesia
comics.summary: Stories written decades later, beginning with Giant-Size Invaders #1 (1975), place Namor in the Invaders beside Captain America, Bucky and the Human Torch, and later in the All-Winners Squad. When the character was revived in the 1950s, Young Men #24 (1953) has Betty Dean call him back to the surface to stop robots claiming to be from Venus that are sinking ships, and he spends the next couple of years fighting communist agents, alien schemers and his envious cousin Byrrah, often alongside his cousin Namora. The era ends in a tragedy told much later: the telepath Destiny uses the Helmet of Power to wipe Namor's memory, and the Sub-Mariner drifts into New York as a nameless vagrant for years.

comics.title: Found in a flophouse
comics.summary: In Fantastic Four #4, Johnny Storm finds a bearded, amnesiac drifter in a Bowery flophouse, burns off his beard and drops him in the river, and the water brings Namor's memory back. Finding his home ruined by atomic testing, he declares war on the surface, sets the sea monster Giganto on New York and becomes infatuated with Sue Storm. He soon joins Doctor Doom against the Fantastic Four only to be betrayed, sides with the Hulk against the Avengers, throws the ice block holding Captain America into the sea (which leads to Cap's revival) and turns down Magneto's offer to join his Brotherhood. Fantastic Four Annual #1 reunites him with his people and Lady Dorma, but when he rescues Sue in the middle of his invasion, Warlord Krang turns Atlantis against him.

comics.title: Trident, memory and loss
comics.summary: In his regular feature in Tales to Astonish, Namor returns home to find Krang on the throne and, freed from the dungeon by Dorma, sets out to find Neptune's Trident, the relic that proves a worthy ruler. In the crossover that launches his own series in 1968, Destiny traps him in ice and shows him the memories he lost, including how his parents met. Sub-Mariner #37 (1971) brings his darkest loss: the Lemurian princess Llyra takes Dorma's place at their wedding to seize the crown, and Dorma, the woman he had legally married, dies before he can save her, leaving Namor nearly mad with grief.

comics.title: A loose team and a formal one
comics.summary: In Marvel Feature #1 (1971) Doctor Strange recruits Namor and the Hulk to stop a doomsday machine, then suggests that the three call themselves the Defenders if they ever regroup; the loose arrangement gave Namor allies without tying him down. Over these years he is briefly reunited with his father, who is later killed on the orders of Tiger Shark and Llyra, and he marries Marrina of Alpha Flight, only to lose her when she turns evil and is killed. In Avengers #262 (1985) Captain America offers him membership and he accepts, sparking a lively rivalry with Hercules, and he is presumed dead when Attuma's forces go to war with the surface in 1989.

comics.title: King in a business suit
comics.summary: Namor turns up behaving erratically in the South Pacific, where marine biologists Caleb and Carrie Alexander work out that his moods swing with an imbalance between air and water in his body. He funds a takeover with sunken treasure, renames the company Oracle, Inc. and sets out to protect the oceans through corporate power, which pits him against the ruthless Marrs twins. Put on trial for his past crimes, he is found guilty but insane and released with Captain America as his probation officer. Later in the run he loses and regains his ankle wings, is stripped of his memory by Master Khan, and is killed by the sorcerer Suma-Ket before the sea god Neptune revives him to defeat Ket.

comics.title: Secrets, civil war and exile
comics.summary: A story set after the Kree-Skrull War reveals Namor as a founder of the Illuminati, the secret council of Iron Man, Mister Fantastic, Professor X, Doctor Strange and Black Bolt, which he insisted be kept hidden. He walks out when the others decide to fire the Hulk into space and again when Stark asks them to back superhero registration, dismissing it as a surface problem. During the Civil War his cousin Namorita is killed in the Stamford battle that sets it off, and he brings an Atlantean army to Captain America's side. Then his long-lost son Kamar tries to provoke a war with the United States, and Namor empties Atlantis, sending his people to live in hiding on land, before Kamar dies when Nitro explodes in the deserted city.

comics.title: Cabal, X-Man and Phoenix
comics.summary: With few friends left, Namor sits on Norman Osborn's secret Cabal beside Doctor Doom, Emma Frost, Loki and the Hood, though he and Doom expect Osborn to fall, and he quits after refusing to execute rogue Atlanteans on Osborn's orders, ending up with the X-Men. With Magneto he builds New Atlantis, a giant pillar that holds up the sinking island of Utopia and gives his scattered people a home, and his own Namor: The First Mutant series pits him against his vampire grandfather Thakorr and drags him to Hell. In Avengers vs. X-Men he becomes one of the Phoenix Five and, defying Cyclops, raises a wall of water that devastates Wakanda and kills untold numbers before the Avengers bring him down.

comics.title: The man who pulled the trigger
comics.summary: Back on the Illuminati as colliding universes threaten Earth, Namor offers T'Challa peace, but Shuri rejects it and Wakanda attacks Atlantis; in reply he sends Thanos's forces to Wakanda with a lie about the Infinity Gems. When neither Mister Fantastic nor Black Panther can bring themselves to destroy an inhabited Earth, Namor does it, then quits and forms a new Cabal with Thanos, Proxima Midnight, Corvus Glaive, Terrax, Black Swan and Maximus to keep destroying other worlds. Sickened by their cruelty, he plots with the Illuminati to trap them, only to be thrown onto a doomed Earth by Black Panther and Black Bolt. He survives into Secret Wars, makes peace with T'Challa on Battleworld and is killed by God Emperor Doom, returning when Reed Richards rebuilds the multiverse.

comics.title: Defenders of the Deep
comics.summary: With Atlantis wrecked, Namor declares war on the surface after a group of starving Atlantean children suffocate on a beach while humans look on, and his new Defenders of the Deep clash with the Avengers. In Invaders a phantom adviser named Machan, wearing the face of a soldier who died in his arms during the war, steers him toward the Omega Sea plan to flood the world and turn humanity into water-breathers, until his old comrade Captain America helps him break free of it. He later fights in the Phoenix's tournament for a new host and loses, his own people rise against him, and after She-Hulk saves Atlantis from a gamma bomb he lets his subjects go and joins the Avengers against the Masters of Evil.

screen.title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
screen.actor: Tenoch Huerta (Manuel Chavez as young Namor)
screen.summary: Namor is introduced as the centuries-old king of Talokan, a hidden Mesoamerican nation under the sea, who kills an American team using a vibranium detector in his waters and then slips into Wakanda to demand that Ramonda and Shuri hand him the student who built it. After Nakia frees Shuri and Riri Williams from his cenote, he floods Birnin Zana, where Ramonda drowns saving Riri, and warns that Wakanda must join his war on the surface or be destroyed. Shuri, now the Black Panther, beats him on a desert beach and tears off one of his ankle wings, and he yields and agrees to a truce, later telling Namora he expects Wakanda to need Talokan one day.

unverified: First appearance: the Marvel Fandom wiki lists Motion Picture Funnies Weekly #1 as the first appearance, with an infobox cover month of June 1939 and a release date of 5 April 1939, while its own notes call the book an unpublished promotional giveaway intended for April 1939. The coverDate field uses the infobox's June 1939. Marvel Comics #1 (October 1939, released 31 August 1939) is his first Marvel/Timely appearance. The MCU Wiki's trivia instead says he was created for Marvel Comics #1 'published in August 1939'.
The Marvel Fandom wiki's account of Funnies Inc. and the book's 1974 rediscovery cites comics.org and Dr. Michael J. Vassallo via the Marvel Mystery Handbook; those outside sources were not checked.

Origin variations: the Expanded History gives several conflicting accounts of how Fen and Leonard McKenzie met and parted (including a 1954 version where Fen hides him in Atlantis and a later claim by Namor, which the wiki treats as suspect, that the relationship was not consensual). The origin keeps to the version in Marvel Comics #1 and the 1968 and 1988 retellings. The Earth-616 page also links the Oracle voyage to a 1915-1920 vibranium hunt tied to Shackleton (Iron Man and Sub-Mariner #1); that layer was left out.
Childhood details (breathing air, strength, ankle wings at 14) come from the Expanded History, which cites Sub-Mariner #35 to #38 (1954-1955); those issue pages were not read.

Marvel Mystery Comics #2 to #7 (the New York rampage, Betty Dean, the trial and the electric chair) rest on the Expanded History; those issue pages were not read. Atlantis Attacks (the 1989 annuals crossover where Namor is presumed dead), the Marrina marriage, the reunion with his father and the Defenders' later years rest on the Earth-616 page alone, which gives no issue citations for most of them. The wiki's Atlantis Attacks Vol 1 page is a 2020 mini-series, not the 1989 event, and was not used.

Invaders membership is a retcon: Giant-Size Invaders #1 is cover-dated June 1975, so the era's years (1953-1955) cover only the 1950s revival issues. The Expanded History also says some of his 1940s adventures were in-universe propaganda comics (Young Allies Comics 70th Anniversary Special); this is not used.

Several issue pages have no plot synopsis, only a solicitation (Sub-Mariner Vol 3 #1 and #6, Namor: The First Mutant #1, Invaders Vol 3 #1 and #12, Avengers Vol 8 #9, #10 and #44). Details from them rest on the Earth-616 character page.

The Earth-616 page's history ends with Avengers Vol 8 #54 (2022). The page's main image is from Namor: Conquered Shores #1, but that series, King in Black: Namor (2020-2021, a flashback to his youth) and anything later are not covered in the history and were left out.

The Earth-616 page cites New Avengers: Illuminati #1 (May 2006), a one-shot, for the Illuminati's founding and for the Hulk-exile and registration meetings; the separate 2007 Illuminati mini-series was not used.

MCU: the MCU Wiki infobox lists Black Panther: Wakanda Forever and Avengers: Doomsday (marked unreleased). Doomsday is left out and was not researched. Namor is not in the Wakanda Forever mid-credits scene described on the film page, and the MCU Wiki's Ironheart (2025) series page does not mention him.
Avengers: Endgame Encore re-release (25 September 2026): the MCU Wiki's Endgame page describes the Encore scenes and Encore-only cast, and neither includes Namor or Talokan, so no entry was added.

Animation is excluded: the MCU Wiki has a zombie Namor variant in the animated Marvel Zombies series (episodes 2 and 4), with a likeness based on Tenoch Huerta. Earlier cartoon appearances were not checked because animation does not count.
No non-MCU live-action Namor was found: the Marvel Fandom disambiguation page lists no film or TV counterpart other than K'uk'ulkan (Earth-199999).

MCU naming: the MCU Wiki gives his birth name as Ch'ah Toh Almehen, sourced to the released script; the Marvel Fandom wiki notes that this comes from the script and may not be firm continuity. His father's background (a Purepécha pochteca spy) and the Tlālōcān naming come from an official podcast cited by the MCU Wiki, not the film. The MCU Wiki's Talokan page says the change from Atlantis was made to avoid comparisons with Aquaman, citing a Screen Rant article; this is not stated as fact in the origin.

The MCU Wiki's behind-the-scenes notes also say Iron Man 2 contains a map 'hot-spot' in the Atlantic and that an Earth-838 Namor was discussed for Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness; neither is an on-screen appearance and both were left out.
